**Steering** is the durable instruction layer an agent loads before it starts work. It establishes the workspace identity, rules, decision process, and core tool-discovery path.

## Bootstrap once

At the beginning of a conversation, call `get_steering`. The response combines:

- current runtime identity;
- current, default, and available node context when the request includes workspace routing information;
- user-owned Markdown from `~/Consuelo/Steering/`;
- tool-discovery guidance;
- the compact core tool manifest.

The call is recorded as an execution. Repeated calls within a short window return loop guards or rate limits instead of duplicating the full context.

## Steering tells the agent where it is

When a workspace can run on more than one node, steering can include the node handling the current request, the workspace default, the available nodes and their presence, and the route source that selected this node.

That context lets an agent reason about requests such as “read the file on my office Mac” without assuming every node has the same filesystem. It also means a default-node change can be visible to new work while an active task remains attached to the node that already owns it.

Use [Nodes](/nodes/) for the product model and [Routing work](/nodes/routing/) for the routing order.

## Load order

Within the local steering directory, OS loads:

1. `system.md` first;
2. any other supported `.md` files in alphabetical order.

`example-system.md`, `decision.md`, and the legacy lowercase file `steering.md` are intentionally ignored.

The runtime does not prepend a repository-owned or bundled system prompt. The visible Steering directory is the source of truth.

## Refresh deliberately

The local snapshot cache fingerprints the Steering directory and its files. Changes, additions, and removals are picked up on the next steering read without restarting Consuelo. An agent that already loaded steering into its current conversation still needs a deliberate refresh or a new conversation to receive the new text.

Read one exact file when only one rule is needed. Use `refresh_steering` only when the workspace instructions have genuinely changed, and include a concrete reason. Refresh calls are also rate limited.

## Steering is not a capability grant

Steering can tell an agent what it should do, but it cannot create a missing tool, widen credentials, or bypass an approval gate. Runtime manifests and security policy remain authoritative for execution.

The same boundary applies to nodes: seeing another node in steering does not make it reachable, online, or authorized for the current call.
